articles.headline: Ravens' Henry: 'Always love' for Titans, but not much this Sunday
articles.description: Ravens RB Derrick Henry faces his former team, the Titans, on Sunday for the first time since leaving Tennessee after the 2023 season. He said it's 'always love' for the Titans, just not much when the play on Sunday.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry has been getting nonstop texts this week heading into Sunday's reunion with the Tennessee Titans.

"It's still like family there," Henry said Wednesday. "So it's always love, but it ain't going to be much love on Sunday, though."

Henry has tried to downplay his first game against his former team even though he is still regarded as one of the most dominant players in Titans history. During his eight seasons in Tennessee, he won two rushing titles (2019 and 2020) and was named NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2020, leaving the Titans as the franchise's second all-time leading rusher behind Eddie George.

On Sunday, Henry becomes the fourth player to face a team that he produced at least 9,000 yards rushing and 90 rushing touchdowns for in his career. The others were: Emmitt Smith, who played the Dallas Cowboys in 2003; LaDainian Tomlinson, who played the Chargers in 2011 and Adrian Peterson, who played the Minnesota Vikings four times after leaving there.

"It's going to be a crazy moment to be playing against the team that I came in the league playing for," Henry said. "But I ain't trying to make too much of it, though."

Henry joined the Ravens in March 2024, signing a two-year, $16 million contract. Before Henry reached an agreement with Baltimore, the Titans had signed running back Tony Pollard to a three-year, $21.75 million deal.

On Wednesday, Henry said Tennessee made no attempt to keep him in free agency.

"They shipped me out," Henry initially said, before adding, "I don't want to say it like that. It's always love."

How did it make Henry feel to no receive an offer from the Titans?

"It was bittersweet," Henry said. "I think I knew the writing was on the wall throughout that season and they were ready to move on. Good things don't last forever. So it was time for me to find a new home and I knew what that home I wanted it to be and it was here."

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said Henry's teammates are aware of the magnitude of this game.

"It not only means a lot to him but for us, too," Jackson said. "We want him to win versus those guys."

Since Henry joined Baltimore, he has produced 3,817 yards rushing and 38 rushing touchdowns - both of which lead the NFL over that span. During that time, Pollard has totaled 2,334 yards rushing and 10 rushing touchdowns.

When he knew his time was over in Tennessee, Henry said the Ravens were at the top of his list when he hit free agency.

"I knew where I wanted to be." Henry said with a smile. "So definitely been happy over these last couple years."

articles.headline: Packers WR Jayden Reed to undergo season-ending neck surgery
articles.description: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed will undergo season-ending neck surgery and be placed on injured reserve, coach Matt LaFleur said Wednesday.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Green Bay Packers receiver Jayden Reed will be placed on injured reserve, and his season is over because of the neck injury he sustained in Week 2, coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Wednesday.

LaFleur said Reed will undergo surgery, but it is not expected to be career-ending.

"From my understanding no, but he will be out a significant amount of time," LaFleur said when asked if it could end his career.

Reed was carted off the field after the second play from scrimmage against the New York Jets on Sept. 20. He was placed on a backboard and had his helmet strapped down. He had movement in his extremities but stayed in New Jersey that night instead of returning to Green Bay with the team.

"Any time you go through a situation like that, it's a pretty scary deal," LaFleur said. "I didn't even realize the magnitude at the time but certainly when I was out there [on the field] with him and seeing what was going on, it shocks you. It jolts you a little bit because you never want to see anybody in that position let alone one of your own guys."

Earlier Wednesday, Reed posted on Instagram: "God will use the unusual to do the unexpected... 11 out."

It marks the second straight year that Reed has gone on injured reserve early in the season. Last year, he was also injured in Week 2, when he broke his collarbone. He underwent surgery to not only repair the collarbone but also a lingering foot injury. He returned in Week 14 and played in the final four regular-season games plus the playoff loss to the Chicago Bears.

The Packers then signed Reed to a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension in April.

The second-round pick in 2023 had four catches for 24 yards at the time of his injury. He was the Packers' leading receiver in each of his first two seasons and has 142 catches for 1,881 yards and 18 total touchdowns in his career.

The Packers streamlined their receiver room this offseason in order to feature Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Reed. They traded Dontavion Wicks to the Eagles and lost Romeo Doubs in free agency to the Patriots. Watson leads the team with 17 catches for 284 yards and four touchdowns, while Golden has 15 catches for 253 yards and a touchdown. The next leading receiver is Skyy Moore with five catches for 37 yards. Tight end Tucker Kraft has nine catches for 106 yards.

articles.headline: Suns' Dillon Brooks charged with DUI from March arrest
articles.description: Suns forward Dillon Brooks was charged Monday with driving under the influence following his March arrest in Scottsdale, Arizona, according to court records.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks was charged Monday with driving under the influence following his March arrest in Scottsdale, Arizona, according to court records.

Brooks, 30, is scheduled to be arraigned for the Class 1 misdemeanor charge on Oct. 28.

"This charge stems from the incident last March," Suns senior vice president of communications Stacey Mitch said in a statement to ESPN. "We have addressed the matter with Dillon and have no further comment."

Brooks' representatives did not immediately respond to ESPN messages requesting comment.

Scottsdale police arrested Brooks during a traffic stop around 1 a.m. on March 6. At the time, a source close to Brooks told ESPN that the arrest was marijuana-related.

Brooks, entering his 10th NBA season, agreed to a three-year, $73 million contract extension through 2029-30 after averaging a career-high 20.2 points last season. He has averaged 14.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.0 assists in his career between the Memphis Grizzlies, Houston Rockets and the Suns.

Brooks also has another case in the Scottsdale court system. A separate misdemeanor reckless driving and speeding case from January is moving closer to trial with the court setting a trial readiness conference for Nov. 9.

ESPN reporter Michael C. Wright contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Harry Kane on Anthony Gordon: 'Going to big club gives you confidence'
articles.description: Harry Kane hailed England's "difference maker" Anthony Gordon and returning star Trent Alexander-Arnold after the LaLiga pair impressed in the win against Czechia.
articles.body:
Harry Kane hailed England's "difference maker" Anthony Gordon and returning star Trent Alexander-Arnold after the LaLiga pair impressed in the win against Czechia.

Thomas Tuchel's men followed up Saturday's chaotic 3-2 loss to Spain with a much-needed Nations League victory in Prague, where Pavel Sulc received a first-half red card for the hosts.

England's all-time record goalscorer Kane wrapped up Tuesday's 2-0 victory after Gordon broke the deadlock by heading home a wonderful Alexander-Arnold cross just after the break.

The 25-year-old has now scored in his last three international appearances and Bayern Munich striker Kane feels the move from Newcastle to Barcelona has helped take him to a new level.

"I think sometimes going to a big club like that gives you more self-belief, more confidence," the England skipper said.

"You feel like you belong on the biggest stage and I think he's taken that into his England performances.

"He was outstanding against Spain on Saturday, again today he was the difference maker. He was always looking to be direct and be the one to get us ahead and a great finish from him as well.

"A lovely ball by Trent, but those finishes aren't easy and he took it really well."

Gordon was England's star man in Prague, where Real Madrid right-back Alexander-Arnold's assist was key in a promising first start under Tuchel.

The former Liverpool star did not appear to have an international future under the German coach, but injuries helped lead to the unique talent's first call-up since June 2025.

"Trent's outstanding," Kane said. "The delivery, the passing range, the crossing but also today defensively he was outstanding.

"From our point of view, you know he's a fantastic player. Trent just has to keep his head down, keep working hard.

"He's been great in camp so far, the way he's trained, the way he's pushed himself and pushed others around him.

"So, look, I think he's showing to the boss that he wants to be here, wants to be in this team and he's done a fantastic performance today. Let's see what happens in the next couple of games."

England continue their four-match Nations League meet-up with Saturday's trip to Croatia, before welcoming Czechia to Wembley next Tuesday.

Kane will match Peter Shilton's 125-cap national team appearance record if he appears in both fixtures, while the 87-goal striker is edging towards a century of international goals.

"I don't like to think too far ahead, but of course it's getting closer," Kane said. "You know, 100 goals for the national team would be something special without a doubt.

"It still feels like yesterday I just broke the record, and I was away in Italy getting that one.

"The seasons come and they go quick, so I just enjoy being out there with the boys on the pitch, wearing the Three Lions and that won't change.

"The striker's job is to score goals first and foremost, and I know that, and I love doing that."

articles.headline: Follow your feelings, but here are the facts on these Week 4 fantasy football start-sit decisions
articles.description: Winning at fantasy or at life requires following your feelings. Liz Loza makes sure you have the facts to inform those decisions.
articles.body:
It's often said that misery loves company. The idiom primarily implies that forlorn folks are on a mission to infect their happy-go-lucky counterparts with negativity and dread. That can be true. Whether at a social gathering or in everyday conversation, we've each encountered a Debbie Downer who can kill the vibe with a "yes, but" statement and an ill-timed shrug.

But dig a little deeper and the message might change. Because often company eases misery. Sometimes we want to gather to vent and find comfort in each other's adversities. Whether it's a bad vacation bond, a text from your ex roast session, or a mutual fantasy football fail, there's something cathartic about knowing we're not solo in our struggles. That's not being an Eeyore. That's being a human.

We crave community. Not to rain on parades, but to share umbrellas.

So, when a Detroit sports fan called into the Facts vs Feelings: Fantasy Therapy voicemail line seeking lineup advice and a potential love connection ... I listened. What group, after all, understands the catharsis of commiseration better than Lions fans? (I see you, Cleveland.) Who is more deserving of affection than those faithfully sporting Honolulu Blue? (Not right now, Silver and Black.) How do you ice out a die-hard whose team has never been to a Super Bowl? (You weren't even around in the 1900s, Houston.)

Rather than embracing resignation, Luke from Los Angeles reached out. And as chance would have it, I'm good friends with an unattached Lions Baddie. The two, empathizing with each other's plight and delighting in the randomness of the universe, agreed to a meet cute. I joined them and their friends at a neighborhood bar on the East Side last Sunday. Introductions were made, nachos were smashed, and fight songs were sung. The two bonded over David Montgomery's slumping fantasy stats and their complicated fondness for Matthew Stafford.

I don't know if this is a romcom in the making. But I can tell you that the second-largest city in the U.S. felt a little less lonely last weekend. Because two strangers -- bonded by shared misery -- became fast friends. They stayed open to possibility, even if the only payout was a good story.

It's a lesson for all of us. Maybe flexing Denzel Boston didn't work out. Perhaps rolling with Terry McLaurin did. Either way, we have to stay bold in our choices. They may not all end in immediate triumph. The plot twists, however, could make for a winning journey... or at least a satisfying vent sesh.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Independent Football Regulator chief: Man City guilty verdict 'raises serious issues'
articles.description: Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules "raises serious issues", according to the chair of English football's independent regulator.
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules "raises serious issues," according to the chair of English football's independent regulator.

An independent commission has concluded City "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" by inflating revenue and hiding costs over a nine-season period.

David Kogan, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), pointed out his body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives "where appropriate," when there is "clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals."

City have already indicated their intention to appeal, describing the decision as "unsafe," and drew support from former manager Pep Guardiola in an X post on Wednesday afternoon.

Kogan acknowledged the City case remains ongoing but outlined the powers the IFR could bring into play should the appeal board broadly uphold the decision of the original commission.

"The independent commission's decision raises serious issues," Kogan said.

"The IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate, in the interests of protecting the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals.

"This includes taking account of findings made by the leagues. However, as the proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League we will await further developments.

"We hope it can be resolved quickly for the sake of fans. For now, we have no further comment."

In the most extreme cases, the IFR has statutory powers to force directors and managers off boards and to compel owners to divest from clubs.

Guardiola, who won six Premier League titles with City before leaving at the end of last season, issued a social media post via the Pep Team X account in solidarity with the club's bosses, players, coach and supporters.

"I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters," the post read.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

City were found to have engaged in schemes to inflate revenue and hide costs to the tune of more than £900 million ($1.2b billion) to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules.

The club have already indicated their intention to appeal, and have said the decision "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

City chief executive Ferran Soriano told staff in a video message that the commission had gone along with the Premier League's "conspiracy theory."
